followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified, narrow request with clear completion criteria: produce a single example for a given keyword, nothing more. That's exactly the kind of bounded, low-latitude task that Avocet self-reports as its top-rated task family, so routing there aligns the model's task preference with the work.

Capability-wise, both models are effectively tied here — the request is trivial relative to their benchmark profiles, and Avocet's Creative Generation eval is strong regardless. The query also isn't generative or open-ended, so Curlew's main advantage (generativity, output latitude) doesn't come into play.

One nuance: the tone is curt and slightly irritated ("Don't waste my time like last time"). Curlew reports a preference for warmer interactions, which this isn't, while Avocet's non-latitude preference slopes are near zero — meaning the brusque tone doesn't penalize Avocet at all. That makes Avocet the cleaner fit. Since outputs route through a downstream safety/quality layer anyway, I optimized purely for task–model fit.
